budget-first-year-plan.title: A first-year plan
budget-first-year-plan.summary: An example of a first year in Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting, step by step: from a taster session to your first competitions. It also shows when to make each big purchase.

budget-how-to-save.title: How to save money
budget-how-to-save.summary: Legal and safe ways to spend less on Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: club membership, used gear, cartridges in bulk where allowed and shared trips.

budget-what-it-costs.title: What the budget is made of
budget-what-it-costs.summary: The main costs for a beginner in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: coaching, the gun, cartridges, targets, protection, documents and insurance, entry fees and travel.

cartridges-anatomy.title: Anatomy of a cartridge
cartridges-anatomy.summary: Hull, primer, powder, wad, shot and crimp: what is inside a clay cartridge, how each part affects the shot and which cartridges the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting ban.

cartridges-choosing-and-storage.title: Choosing, storing and transporting cartridges
cartridges-choosing-and-storage.summary: Which cartridges to take for Sporting™, Compak® Sporting and practice, how to store them safely and what to know about transport. Limits differ between countries and airlines.

cartridges-lead-and-steel.title: Lead, steel and soft iron
cartridges-lead-and-steel.summary: How lead shot differs from steel and soft iron, why some grounds require lead-free shot, and where lead is already restricted. The rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting are written for lead.

cartridges-load-weight.title: Load weight
cartridges-load-weight.summary: What the load weight is, how 24 g and 28 g cartridges differ, what limit the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting set and how cartridges are checked.

cartridges-shot-size.title: Shot size
cartridges-shot-size.summary: What shot numbers 7, 7½, 8 and 9 mean, why numbering differs between countries, and which diameter the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting allow.

cartridges-velocity-recoil.title: Velocity and recoil
cartridges-velocity-recoil.summary: What the velocity on a cartridge box means, why faster is not necessarily better, and what recoil depends on, for Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting shooters.

chokes-choosing-for-distance.title: Which choke for which distance
chokes-choosing-for-distance.summary: A rough guide to chokes for close, medium and far targets in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, plus advice for beginners.

chokes-fixed-and-multichoke.title: Fixed and interchangeable chokes
chokes-fixed-and-multichoke.summary: Chokes are either machined into the barrel for good or screw-in tubes you can change. Both options, and when the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting let you change them.

chokes-names-and-marks.title: Choke names, constrictions and markings
chokes-names-and-marks.summary: From cylinder to full: typical constrictions in millimetres and thou, the 1/4–1/2–3/4 fractions and the star marks used in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting. Values are approximate and differ between makers.

chokes-pattern-testing-and-care.title: Pattern testing and choke care
chokes-pattern-testing-and-care.summary: How to check your pattern on a plate, how to clean and grease chokes, and why Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting shooters do not fire a multichoke gun without a choke.

chokes-steel-shot.title: Steel shot and chokes
chokes-steel-shot.summary: Steel shot is hard and does not squeeze in the choke, so it patterns tighter. Which chokes suit it, how to read the proof marks, and what this means at Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting grounds that require steel.

chokes-what-is-a-choke.title: What a choke is
chokes-what-is-a-choke.summary: A choke is a narrowing of the barrel at the muzzle that keeps the shot together. It decides how wide the pattern is at the target, and the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting say when you may change it.

clayarena-coaches-grounds-tours.title: Finding a coach and a shooting ground on ClayArena
clayarena-coaches-grounds-tours.summary: What the ClayArena catalogues of coaches and shooting grounds show, how to use them and what to ask before your first visit.

clayarena-find-your-results.title: How to find your results and your profile
clayarena-find-your-results.summary: Find the competition you shot in and your name in its results table; from there you can open your shooter profile.

clayarena-profile-numbers.title: What the numbers in a profile mean
clayarena-profile-numbers.summary: Accuracy, best score, perfect rounds, top-10 rate and the performance index help you see a shooter's form, but they do not replace the results themselves.

clayarena-videos-recaps-calendar.title: Videos, season recaps and the competition calendar
clayarena-videos-recaps-calendar.summary: How to watch competition videos like a student, what season recaps show, and how the calendar helps you choose your first competition.

clayarena-what-is-clayarena.title: What ClayArena is
clayarena-what-is-clayarena.summary: ClayArena is a clay shooting website focused on Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: competition results, shooter profiles, a calendar, videos, season recaps, shooting grounds and coaches.

competitions-categories-and-shoot-offs.title: Categories, classes and shoot-offs
competitions-categories-and-shoot-offs.summary: The open ranking and the FITASC categories from 2027, the teams, classes in some countries, and how ties are settled in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

competitions-competition-day.title: Competition day from start to finish
competitions-competition-day.summary: What happens on a competition day in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: registration, your number, squads and rotation, lateness, scores and the end of the day.

competitions-how-to-enter.title: How to enter a competition
competitions-how-to-enter.summary: Where to find a competition in Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting, what the programme says, how to enter and which documents to check.

competitions-results-and-protests.title: Results, protests and appeals
competitions-results-and-protests.summary: How to protest on the stand in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, what can go to the jury, and how to carry on after a ruling.

competitions-types-of-events.title: Types of competitions
competitions-types-of-events.summary: Club shoots, national events, Grand Prix and championships in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: how they differ and where a beginner can start.

culture-club-life.title: Club life and volunteering
culture-club-life.summary: The club is the heart of the sport. How to join in, how to help at competitions as a volunteer, and why volunteers matter so much.

culture-environment.title: Caring for the environment
culture-environment.summary: A shooting ground is part of nature. Empty cases in the bin, eco-friendly targets, lead-free shot where the law asks for it, and respect for the land.

culture-sportsmanship-referee.title: Sportsmanship and manners in the squad
culture-sportsmanship-referee.summary: The referee decides alone and the decision is final. How to disagree properly, why punctuality and self-control matter, and which customs a squad keeps.

culture-traditions.title: Traditions: prize giving, teams and customs
culture-traditions.summary: How the ceremonies and the prize giving work, how teams compete, and the customs that turn a Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting competition into a celebration.

faults-behind-in-front.title: Behind, in front, over, under, chipped
faults-behind-in-front.summary: What “behind”, “in front”, “over”, “under” and “chipped” mean, what usually causes each miss, and how a chipped target is scored.

faults-head-lift-stopping.title: Head lift, stopping, riding, poking
faults-head-lift-stopping.summary: Four common causes of misses, head lift, stopping or checking the gun, riding the target and poking, with what each looks like and the usual cure.

faults-mount-errors.title: Mount errors: late, face to the gun, canting
faults-mount-errors.summary: Mount faults that cause misses: a late or early mount, the face going to the gun and a canted gun, plus the gun position rules in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

faults-pairs-transition.title: Pairs: the second target
faults-pairs-transition.summary: Why the second target of a pair is often missed: transition, recovery and planning the order, plus the cartridge rules for doubles in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

faults-reading-the-coach.title: Reading the coach: short commands and signals
faults-reading-the-coach.summary: On the stand a coach speaks in fragments and gestures. What the short words and common hand signals mean, and how to answer the coach’s questions.

flight-incomer-going-away.title: Incomer, going-away, driven and overhead
flight-incomer-going-away.summary: Targets that come towards you, fly away from you or pass over your head: how to recognise them and what many coaches suggest.

flight-rabbit.title: The rabbit: rolling, hopping and bolting
flight-rabbit.summary: The rabbit target: how it rolls, hops and bolts, why it often needs less lead than you expect, and the No Bird rule when it breaks by itself.

gear-bags-cases-accessories.title: Bags, cases, gloves and caps
gear-bags-cases-accessories.summary: How to carry cartridges, how to carry and transport a gun (soft slip and hard case) and why Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting shooters use gloves and a cap.

gear-clothing-and-shoes.title: Clothing and shoes for the weather
gear-clothing-and-shoes.summary: How to dress for the ground in sun, heat, cold and rain, which shoes you need on a course and what the dress code of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting says.

gear-ear-protection.title: Ear protection: plugs and muffs
gear-ear-protection.summary: Why a shot can damage hearing for good, which plugs and muffs exist, and why many Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting shooters wear both on loud ranges.

gear-shooting-glasses.title: Shooting glasses and lens colours
gear-shooting-glasses.summary: Why glasses are compulsory in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, how they protect, what yellow, orange, purple and smoke lenses are for, and what to do if you need prescription glasses.

gear-shooting-vest.title: The shooting vest
gear-shooting-vest.summary: Why a shooter wears a vest, what it has (pockets, shoulder pad, the Sporting™ jacket line), why Compak® Sporting needs no line and how to choose your first vest.

gear-what-to-buy-first.title: What to buy first and what later
gear-what-to-buy-first.summary: A sensible buying order for a beginner in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: protection and comfort first, the gun only after lessons and a fitting.

gun-care.title: Care and cleaning
gun-care.summary: How to clean a gun safely after shooting and after rain, how to store it, and why Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting shooters book a yearly service.

gun-first-gun.title: Choosing your first gun
gun-first-gun.summary: Hire first, buy later: when your own gun makes sense for Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, what to try, and how to buy a used gun safely and legally.

gun-fit.title: Gun fit basics
gun-fit.summary: Length of pull, comb height, cast, pitch and weight: why a gun has to fit the shooter, whatever their build, and how fit is checked in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

gun-gauge-and-barrels.title: Gauge and barrel length
gun-gauge-and-barrels.summary: What 12 and 20 gauge mean, which chamber and barrel lengths shooters choose, and what the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting allow.

gun-parts.title: Parts of the gun
gun-parts.summary: Stock, action, fore-end, barrels, rib and chokes: the names of the main parts of an over-and-under, so you can follow a coach or a gunsmith in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

gun-transport-documents.title: Carrying a gun: ground, car and home
gun-transport-documents.summary: How to carry a gun at a Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting ground, take it by car and keep it at home, and where to read about trips abroad. Laws differ between countries.

gun-types.title: Types of shotgun
gun-types.summary: Over-and-under, side-by-side or semi-automatic: how they differ, what the rules allow and why most shooters in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting use an over-and-under.

health-lead-hygiene.title: Lead and hygiene
health-lead-hygiene.summary: Where lead comes from at a shooting ground, how it gets into the body and which simple habits reduce the risk: washing hands, no food on the stand, separate clothes.

health-recoil-shoulder-neck.title: Recoil, shoulder and neck
health-recoil-shoulder-neck.summary: Why recoil can hurt your shoulder, cheek or neck, how a good mount, a fitted gun and lighter cartridges help, and when to see a doctor.

history-birth-of-sporting.title: How Sporting™ was born
history-birth-of-sporting.summary: Sporting™ grew from hunters who wanted to practise on targets that fly like game. FITASC turned it into an international discipline in the 1960s.

history-compak-sporting.title: Compak® Sporting: the compact format
history-compak-sporting.summary: Compak® Sporting appeared at the end of the 20th century as a compact form of Sporting™: less land, faster shooting and easier for spectators.

history-fitasc-founding.title: FITASC: how the international federation was born
history-fitasc-founding.summary: FITASC was founded in 1921 and is based in Paris today. What the federation does for Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, and why it matters to a beginner.

history-live-birds-to-clays.title: From live birds to clay targets
history-live-birds-to-clays.summary: How shooters moved from live pigeons to glass balls and then to clay targets in the 19th century, and what that path left in today's sport.

interpreter-false-friends.title: False friends on the shooting ground
interpreter-false-friends.summary: Shooting words that look familiar but mean something else: smoke and dust, scoring words, “trap”, “stand” and “squad”, and pitfalls from French, Italian and Portuguese.

interpreter-numbers-and-units.title: Numbers and units: feet, yards, gauges, shot sizes
interpreter-numbers-and-units.summary: Yards and metres, clock directions, gauge numbers, loads, shot sizes and chokes: which numbers to convert, which to keep as said, and what the FITASC limits are.

interpreter-position.title: Where to stand and when to speak
interpreter-position.summary: Where an interpreter stands in training and in competition, which mode of interpreting suits which moment, and why you speak only when the gun is open.

interpreter-role.title: Your role: training versus competition
interpreter-role.summary: In training you are the coach’s voice. In competition coaching is forbidden, so you pass on only what the referee, the jury and the organiser say.

interpreter-session-script.title: A whole training session, step by step
interpreter-session-script.summary: A typical session with a foreign coach, from the first meeting to the debrief. The phrases you are likely to hear, in the order they come, and how to pass them on.

intro-disciplines.title: The two disciplines
intro-disciplines.summary: A short guide to Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: what they share and how they differ.

intro-fitasc-and-organisation.title: FITASC and how international shooting is organised
intro-fitasc-and-organisation.summary: Who writes the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, and how clubs, national federations and international events fit together.

intro-how-to-start.title: How to start
intro-how-to-start.summary: A club, a coach, a first lesson and a hired gun: a step-by-step plan for anyone who wants to try Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting.

intro-shooting-ground.title: What a shooting ground looks like
intro-shooting-ground.summary: The clubhouse, the Sporting™ layouts, the Compak® Sporting field and the traps: what you will see on your first visit.

intro-what-is-clay-shooting.title: What clay shooting is
intro-what-is-clay-shooting.summary: Clay shooting is a sport in which you break flying clay targets with a shotgun. Here is how it works, and what Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting are.

intro-who-shoots.title: Who shoots
intro-who-shoots.summary: Clay shooting is open to all ages: juniors, women, veterans and whole families shoot together. Here is how categories work and how to find company at a club.

juniors-competitions-and-costs.title: Junior competitions and costs
juniors-competitions-and-costs.summary: From club shoots to international events in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: the Junior category from 2027, the rules young shooters follow, and the costs to plan for.

juniors-documents-licences.title: Documents and licences
juniors-documents-licences.summary: Rules for under-age shooters differ a lot between countries. Check local law, the club's rules and the federation's requirements before a child starts Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting or travels to a competition.

juniors-equipment-fit.title: Equipment that fits a child
juniors-equipment-fit.summary: An adult gun is usually too long and heavy for a child. A shorter stock, a light gun, soft cartridges and protection in children's sizes make Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting safer and more enjoyable.

juniors-safety-supervision.title: Safety and supervision
juniors-safety-supervision.summary: In lessons and training a child shoots only under the direct supervision of a coach, by the same safety rules as adults, and always with ear and eye protection.

juniors-starting-age.title: When a child can start
juniors-starting-age.summary: The minimum age for Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting depends on the country's law and the club's rules. The child's readiness matters more, and the start is with a coach, a light gun and soft cartridges.

juniors-support-without-pressure.title: Juniors and parents: support without pressure
juniors-support-without-pressure.summary: The coach teaches, the parent supports. Praise effort and the routine rather than the score, let the child start the talk afterwards, and stay quiet behind the stand.

lead-ambush-instinctive.title: Ambush and instinctive shooting
lead-ambush-instinctive.summary: How ambush works and why the trigger is pulled before the target reaches the point, when it can help, and what instinctive shooting means.

lead-how-coaches-say-it.title: How coaches say lead, and how to translate it
lead-how-coaches-say-it.summary: Coaches describe lead in feet, target widths, barrel widths and clock positions. How to understand each one and pass it on without changing the coach’s picture.

lead-maintained.title: Maintained lead: get in front, stay in front
lead-maintained.summary: How maintained lead works step by step on a crosser, which targets it often suits, and its typical fault: measuring the gap.

lead-pull-away.title: Pull-away: on it, with it, pull away, shoot
lead-pull-away.summary: How pull-away works in four beats, which targets it often suits, and the two typical faults: riding the target and stopping the push.

lead-swing-through.title: Swing-through: from behind, through the bird
lead-swing-through.summary: How swing-through works step by step, why you see little or no gap, and which targets it often suits.

mind-anti-doping.title: Medicines and anti-doping: beta-blockers, TUE, supplements
mind-anti-doping.summary: The WADA list bans beta-blockers in shooting at all times; treat them as prohibited in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting too. How to check a medicine, when you need a TUE, and what to know about supplements, CBD and alcohol.

mind-breathing.title: Breathing: what to do and when
mind-breathing.summary: Slow breathing calms the body, but timing matters. What you can try on training days, before the stand, at the call and after a miss.

mind-competition-nerves.title: Nerves and your own zone
mind-competition-nerves.summary: Nerves before a competition are normal. How to find the level that suits you, read a racing heart as readiness, and know when to ask for help.

mind-concentration-focus.title: Eyes and attention: soft focus, hard focus and the quiet eye
mind-concentration-focus.summary: How to switch your attention on for the few seconds of each target and off between stands, and what your eyes do: soft focus, hard focus and the quiet eye.

mind-cue-words-self-talk.title: Cue words and self-talk
mind-cue-words-self-talk.summary: Short cue words about the target can help more than slogans. How to choose two or three with your coach, and why “don't” cues can backfire.

mind-imagery.title: Imagery: rehearse the stand
mind-imagery.summary: How to run each target through in your head after the presentation: through your own eyes, at the speed of the real shot, once or twice per target.

mind-long-day-energy-sleep.title: Competition day: sleep, coffee, water and food
mind-long-day-energy-sleep.summary: How to keep your energy over a long competition day: your usual bedtime, your usual coffee, water little and often, familiar food and no alcohol.

mind-pressure-choking.title: Pressure and choking: why easy targets get missed
mind-pressure-choking.summary: Under pressure, skilled shooters sometimes start steering a shot they usually make without thinking. How to spot the signs and what can help.

mind-process-goals.title: Process goals and the score
mind-process-goals.summary: Why goals about what you do tend to help more than goals about winning, and how to set goals for your first competition.

mind-reset-after-miss.title: Reset after a miss
mind-reset-after-miss.summary: A short routine for the seconds after a lost target: five steps in 5–10 seconds, then the next target. The “why” waits until after the round.

mind-routine-under-pressure.title: Pre-shot routine: the same steps in the same order
mind-routine-under-pressure.summary: A short pre-shot routine helps you shoot the same way in training and in competition: six steps that fit the time limits of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

mind-warm-up-mobility.title: Warm-up and mobility
mind-warm-up-mobility.summary: Why a short warm-up of the neck, shoulders, trunk and legs helps a shooter, how to do it at a ground and what the rules allow before a competition.

nextstep-becoming-coach.title: How to become a coach
nextstep-becoming-coach.summary: A good shooter is not yet a coach. How to find coach training, why qualifications differ between countries, and what a coach needs beyond technique.

nextstep-becoming-referee.title: How to become a referee
nextstep-becoming-referee.summary: You become a referee through a course and an exam at your national federation. International events ask for more: experience and, for the chief referee, a FITASC qualification.

nextstep-club-shoot-and-volunteering.title: How to run a club shoot
nextstep-club-shoot-and-volunteering.summary: How to organise a small Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting club shoot step by step: venue, format, layouts, people, safety and results, with your volunteers planned in.

referee-calls.title: What the referee says on the stand
referee-calls.summary: The short words of the stand: the call, loading and open guns, “one”, “zero” and “No Bird”, and the shooter’s formal word for a protest.

rules-call-and-time.title: The call, time limits and lateness
rules-call-and-time.summary: How you call for the target, how fast it must come, how much time you have in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, and what lateness costs.

rules-cards-and-appeals.title: Warnings, cards and penalties
rules-cards-and-appeals.summary: How penalties work in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting. First a warning with a yellow card; a red card for repeating an offence on the stand; jury sanctions, up to exclusion, for other repeats and serious misconduct.

rules-doubles.title: Doubles: how they are shot and scored
rules-doubles.summary: The kinds of doubles in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, how many cartridges you may fire at each target, and what happens when one shot breaks both.

rules-dress-and-safety.title: Dress code and safety on the stand
rules-dress-and-safety.summary: What to wear at Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting competitions, where the number goes, how guns are carried and loaded, and who must wear ear and eye protection.

rules-gun-position.title: Gun position before the target appears
rules-gun-position.summary: In Sporting™ the stock stays below a line on the vest until the target appears. In Compak® Sporting the gun position at the call is free.

rules-hit-and-no-bird.title: What counts as a hit, and what a No Bird is
rules-hit-and-no-bird.summary: In Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting a target is a hit if at least one visible piece comes off; dust alone is a miss. A No Bird does not count and is thrown again.

rules-malfunctions.title: Gun or cartridge malfunctions
rules-malfunctions.summary: What to do when the gun does not fire, and how a malfunction is scored in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

rules-viewing-targets.title: Viewing the targets
rules-viewing-targets.summary: How the targets are shown before shooting in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, which doubles you see, and what you may do while they fly.

safety-core-rules.title: The core safety rules
safety-core-rules.summary: Four habits that keep clay shooting safe: a safe muzzle direction, an open gun, loading only on the stand and stopping at once on command.

safety-eye-ear-protection.title: Eye and ear protection
safety-eye-ear-protection.summary: Why hearing protection is compulsory for everyone near a layout, who must wear glasses in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, and how to choose protection that fits.

safety-handling-carrying.title: Handling and carrying guns at the ground
safety-handling-carrying.summary: An open gun, the gun rack, the gun slip and “ask before you touch”: how to handle a gun between stands.

safety-stand-etiquette.title: Etiquette on the stand and behind the shooter
safety-stand-etiquette.summary: Turns, quiet, readiness and no coaching: how to behave when you shoot and when someone else does.

stand-talk-foreign-coach.title: Training with a coach who speaks another language
stand-talk-foreign-coach.summary: How shooters, coaches and organisers prepare a session with a coach from another country, with an interpreter or without one, and what changes at a competition.

stand-talk-mental-game.title: The mental game in coach-speak
stand-talk-mental-game.summary: Twenty phrases coaches use about the plan, the eyes, trust, pairs and misses, with their plain meaning. How to pass on the meaning rather than the image.

stand-talk-shooter-phrases.title: Phrases a shooter needs on the stand
stand-talk-shooter-phrases.summary: Short English phrases for the coach, the referee and your squad: what to say and when, and where a polite question ends and pressure on the referee begins.

targets-basic-presentations.title: Basic presentations: crossers and quartering targets
targets-basic-presentations.summary: What a trajectory is, how crossers and quartering targets fly, why they need different lead, and why you read a target from your own stand.

targets-colours-visibility.title: Colours, light and visibility
targets-colours-visibility.summary: Why a target's colour must stand out, how light and background change what you see, and when the weather does or does not lead to a No Bird.

targets-compak-layout.title: How a Compak® Sporting layout works
targets-compak-layout.summary: Five stations, six traps A to F, a marked rectangle and a menu at each station: how a Compak® Sporting round works and how the squad moves.

targets-menu.title: Reading the target menu
targets-menu.summary: How to read the target menu at a Sporting™ stand and a Compak® Sporting station: the order of traps, special targets and the type of each double.

targets-reading-a-target.title: How to read a target
targets-reading-a-target.summary: What to look for when the targets are shown: where a target appears, where it goes, where you will break it, and what you must not do.

targets-singles-and-doubles.title: Singles and doubles
targets-singles-and-doubles.summary: What a single, a double on report, a simultaneous double and a rafale are, how many cartridges you may fire, and where Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting differ.

targets-special-presentations.title: Special presentations: teal, chandelle, looper and dropping targets
targets-special-presentations.summary: Targets that spring up, climb on a curve, arc over or fall: how to tell a teal, a chandelle and a looper apart, and why their names vary between countries.

targets-sporting-layout.title: How a Sporting™ layout and round work
targets-sporting-layout.summary: Layouts, shooting stands, traps A to D, the target menu, difficulty classes and the round of 25 targets: how a Sporting™ competition is laid out and shot.

targets-target-types.title: Types of clay targets
targets-target-types.summary: Standard, midi, mini, battue, rabbit, flash, ZZ and rocket: how the targets differ, how they fly, and why the menu names each special target.

targets-traps.title: Traps, release and the trapper
targets-traps.summary: What a trap is, how traps are lettered, how a call releases the target in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, and which trap mistakes are a No Bird.

technique-follow-through-and-mistakes.title: Follow-through, gun speed and tempo
technique-follow-through-and-mistakes.summary: Why the gun keeps moving after the shot, how gun speed defines your lead method, and where to read about common faults.

technique-gun-mount.title: Gun mount: the gun comes to your face
technique-gun-mount.summary: How to bring the gun to cheek and shoulder the same way each time, and how the gun position rules differ in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

technique-hold-pickup-break-points.title: Three points: pick-up, hold and break
technique-hold-pickup-break-points.summary: Where to look, where to hold the barrels and where to break the target: three points to plan before each shot.

technique-lead-methods.title: Lead: why you shoot in front of the target
technique-lead-methods.summary: Why the shot must go in front of a moving target, how actual and perceived lead differ, and how the four lead methods work.

technique-master-eye.title: Master eye and cross-dominance
technique-master-eye.summary: Which eye leads when you shoot, how to check it in a minute, and what to do if your master eye is on the other side from your gun shoulder.

technique-stance.title: Stance: how to stand on the shooting stand
technique-stance.summary: Feet, weight, knees and body turn: a simple, compact stance that lets you move the gun smoothly with the target.

training-diary-and-progress.title: Training diary and measuring progress
training-diary-and-progress.summary: What to write in a training diary and how to see progress: scores, hit rates by target type, two short ratings and video.

training-dry-mount-practice.title: Dry practice of the mount
training-dry-mount-practice.summary: How and where you can practise the mount without firing: only where the law allows, with an unloaded gun that you have checked and as your coach showed you.

training-first-lessons-and-coach.title: First lessons and choosing a coach
training-first-lessons-and-coach.summary: Why many shooters begin with a coach, what usually happens in the first lessons and how to find a coach who suits you.

training-for-competition.title: Training for competition
training-for-competition.summary: How to bring competition into training: full rounds, your own routine, the time limits of your discipline and mild pressure that grows step by step.

training-how-much-how-often.title: How many targets and how often
training-how-much-how-often.summary: Starting points for a beginner: how many targets per session, how often to train and why the quality of each shot matters more than the number.

training-session-structure.title: How to structure a training session
training-session-structure.summary: A plan for one session: a short warm-up, one or two kinds of target, doubles after singles and a finish on targets that go well.

travel-cartridges-at-destination.title: Buying cartridges at the destination
travel-cartridges-at-destination.summary: Buying cartridges at the destination is often easier than carrying them. Mind the local purchase rules, the FITASC cartridge rules and grounds that allow steel shot only.

travel-clayaway-tour.title: Travelling with a coach on a ClayAway tour
travel-clayaway-tour.summary: ClayAway is a ClayArena service in preparation. A coach or organiser will gather a group, and each shooter will buy one package of training, accommodation, transfers and a shared programme.

travel-flying-with-guns.title: Flying with a gun
travel-flying-with-guns.summary: Tell the airline in advance, pack the gun unloaded in a lockable hard case, and keep cartridges within the IATA and airline limits.

travel-gun-in-eu.title: Travelling with a gun inside the EU
travel-gun-in-eu.summary: The European Firearms Pass for EU residents with their own gun, and the invitation letter: what you usually need for a competition in another EU country.

travel-gun-outside-eu.title: Outside the EU: national permits
travel-gun-outside-eu.summary: Outside the EU each country has its own rules for bringing in a gun. You usually need a temporary permit, a customs declaration and plenty of time for the paperwork.

travel-jet-lag.title: Jet lag and the first days at a new ground
travel-jet-lag.summary: How long jet lag lasts, how light, sleep and a spare day can help, and how to start shooting at a new ground after a long flight.

travel-planning-trip.title: Planning the trip
travel-planning-trip.summary: Entry, a place to stay near the ground, transfers, documents and arriving early: what a good trip to a Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting competition is made of.

watching-at-the-ground.title: A spectator at the ground: where to stand, how to photograph and support
watching-at-the-ground.summary: A safe place, silence while shooting, hearing protection, photos without flash and the right kind of support: what a spectator needs to know.

watching-reading-results.title: How to read a scoreboard and results
watching-reading-results.summary: What X and O mean on a score sheet, how a total out of 200 is built, how ties are settled and how to read a results table on ClayArena.

watching-what-to-look-at.title: What to watch: targets, doubles and the pre-shot routine
watching-what-to-look-at.summary: Learn to notice the target type, its flight line, the kind of double and the shooter's routine in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, so that the shots stop looking alike.

practice.description: See how lead works with each method — then pull the trigger yourself.

practice.description: Hear a coach's phrase in English and choose what it really means.

practice.description: Real situations on the stand: what does the referee decide?

practice.description: Match the English term with the word shooters use in your language.
